speaker_role: independent counselor (Ethan Sawyer, College Essay Guy)
commercial_incentive: Promotes CollegeEssayGuy.com resources (free downloadable verb list, guide) and channel subscription; no direct paid pitch in this video
key_insights: Common App activity descriptions are limited to 150 characters, so word choice matters a lot; vague descriptions waste that space.
Using strong, specific active verbs (e.g., 'organized,' 'brainstormed,' 'spearheaded') instead of generic ones ('worked,' 'helped') conveys much more about what a student actually did.
Recommends a 'brainstorm exercise' per activity covering: what you did (verbs), problems you solved, lessons/skills gained, impact/who you affected, and how you applied those lessons elsewhere.
Suggests doing a 'values scan' after drafting descriptions — checking whether each entry reveals a distinct personal value, and cutting redundant entries that repeat the same value.
Warns against fabricating or exaggerating activities; cites a case where a student lied about a leadership title and a trip, was caught via inconsistencies, and had offers rescinded.
For awards/honors, advises listing in order of importance, explaining what an obscure award actually is, quantifying selectivity (e.g., how many competitors), and explaining unfamiliar acronyms.

States there is no single right answer on whether to list every activity versus only the most significant ones — reasonable counselors differ, and either approach ('completeness' vs. 'quality over quantity') is defensible.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Common App activity descriptions are capped at 150 characters, per the video.
notable_or_distinctive: The structured 'brainstorm exercise' (what/problems solved/lessons/impact/application) and the follow-up 'values scan' technique for auditing an already-drafted activities list are more concrete and reusable than typical generic tips.
reliability_notes: Independent counselor content, generally practical and non-salesy in this video, though it promotes free resources on his own site; advice is opinion-based (e.g., on quality vs. quantity) rather than sourced from official admissions data, and auto-captions render 'BB's exercise' oddly (stands for 'best extracurricular activity brainstorm').
